title: spec: jmap-chat-push 'properties is authoritative: exactly the requested fields' is unsatisfiable
description:
Found 2026-11-23 reading draft-atwood-jmap-chat-push-00 before
implementing it (bead mimid-1wgh.99). Mark's own draft; needs his call.

THE SENTENCE, §chat-push-config line 127:

  "The `properties` list is authoritative: the server returns exactly
   the requested fields."

It cannot be obeyed. Five other rules in the same document require a
requested field to be absent:

1. line 189 `hasMention`      "MUST be absent when `encrypted` is `true`"
2. line 192 `mentionScopes`   "MUST be absent when `encrypted` is `true`"
3. line 195 `bodySnippet`     "When `true`, `bodySnippet` MUST be absent"
4. line 171 `chatName`        "Absent for `direct` chats"
5. lines 174, 177 `spaceId`, `spaceName`  "Absent for other kinds"

And the DEFAULT `properties` set named in that same sentence includes
`hasMention`, `mentionScopes` and `bodySnippet`. So a server using the
document's own default, delivering an encrypted message, is required to
return exactly those fields and required to omit three of them. Every
E2EE deployment hits this on its first push, which for mimid is every
push.

THE SECOND, SHARPER PROBLEM: `encrypted` is filterable.

`encrypted` is declared `(Boolean)` at line 194, not optional, so it is
structurally present in every entry -- yet it is governed by
`properties` like everything else, so a client may leave it out. A
client that does gets an entry with no `bodySnippet` and no way to tell
whether the body was encrypted or merely had no snippet. That is the one
field whose absence changes how every other field is read, and it is the
one the draft lets a client discard.

THE FIX IS ALREADY IN THE DRAFT, as a pattern. `unreadCount` (line 186)
says it "is a property of the push as a whole, not of any one entry, and
is not governed by the `properties` list of {{chat-push-config}}". So
the document already knows how to exempt a field.

PROPOSED, for Mark:
- Make `properties` an upper bound rather than an exact set: "the server
  returns no field the list does not name; a field the list names is
  present only when the rules for that field allow it", and point at
  §e2ee and the kind-conditional fields.
- Exempt `encrypted` from `properties` the way `unreadCount` is
  exempted, so a client cannot ask for a payload it cannot interpret.
  Alternatively require that `encrypted` be included whenever
  `bodySnippet`, `hasMention` or `mentionScopes` is requested, but the
  exemption is simpler and harder to get wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: "returns exactly the requested fields"
is the kind of sentence an implementer tests against. Two conforming
servers will differ on the encrypted case -- one omitting the three
fields, one emitting nulls to honour "exactly" -- and clients will be
written against whichever they met first.

Not posted anywhere. Fixing the draft is a write to ~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec,
which AGENTS.md says needs Mark's approval per write.
notes: FIXED 2026-11-23 in jmap-chat-spec commit 377bddb, Mark approved. 'properties' is now an upper bound rather than an exact set, naming the five cases a client cannot predict when it sets the list: hasMention, mentionScopes and bodySnippet under encryption, chatName for a direct Chat, spaceId and spaceName off a channel. And 'encrypted' is taken out of the properties list and made present in every entry, following the precedent already in the draft for unreadCount, so a client can always tell an absence caused by encryption from one it did not request. The default properties set no longer names encrypted, since it is unconditional. Renders clean.
